notes: Expected brightness is only marginal: W2 13.9 (about 0.47 mJy) gives an expected S/N of about 2 to 3 per visit.
A faint background star (AllWISE J085501.95-071428.1, W2 15.05, about 0.16 mJy) sits about 1.3 pixels from the 2025-26 position, inside the measuring aperture, so any signal here is blended.

Noise checked 2026-11-14: an earlier build reported S/N 8.1 and 7.9 from the stack's per-pixel spread x sqrt(N), which ignores that reprojection correlates neighbouring pixels. The same aperture at about 1000 blank positions per stack scatters 1.65 to 1.74x more, matching the frame-to-frame scatter within each visit (0.16, 0.12, 0.11 vs 0.19, 0.14, 0.12 in stack units), so S/N is 2.0, 5.1 and 4.9. Single-frame VARIANCE errors match their own blank-sky scatter (median ratio 1.1): the photometry errors stand.
Not separately detected in any visit: the one stack over S/N 5 (Nov 2025, 5.1) includes the background star, and without it would be about 4. No star marker is drawn.
2 of 3 visits (2025-05-05, 2025-11-19) are not at the shared wavelength (4.730 um, colour_matched false): in a flipbook their brightness changes from colour alone.

Detection: forced S/N in a 2 px aperture on the stack against the scatter of the same aperture at blank positions of that stack (reprojection correlates pixels, so a per-pixel noise would overstate S/N); needs S/N 5 and the centre within 1.5 px of the prediction.
Each frame saw a different wavelength at the star's pixel (ranges per visit); a brightness change between visits mixes real change with colour. Not a light curve.
Per visit, only frames with no masked pixel in the aperture are averaged (frames_used); 0 visits had none, so their sums are lower limits.
Photometry: forced 3 px (18.5 arcsec) radius aperture sum on each frame, local sky annulus, VARIANCE errors, no aperture correction, mean per visit.

target.name: WISE 0855-0714
target.claim: Not separately detected: about 2 sigma per visit in forced photometry (0.39 +/- 0.20, 0.67 +/- 0.28 and 0.31 +/- 0.14 mJy; S/N 2.0, 5.1 and 4.9 in the visit stacks), consistent with the expected 0.47 mJy plus a blended background star.
target.astrometry_source: Not in Gaia (a Y dwarf, far too faint in G). J2000 position, proper motion and parallax from SIMBAD (Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7). The challenge coordinates 08h55m10.831s -7d14m42.53s are the WISE All-Sky position at epoch 2010.338, not J2000: see pipeline/blink/WISE0855_NOTES.md.
